findings.cloud_extension: Scovant Cloud tests reachability from real agent network paths and multiple regions.
findings.limitations: Scovant Core evaluates declared and static evidence only; it does not observe real agent traffic.
findings.remediation: Collapse the redirect chain to at most one hop.
findings.summary: The entry URL redirects 4 times before settling.
findings.title: HTTPS reachability
findings.why_it_matters: An agent that cannot complete a request against the entry URL cannot use anything else the site declares.

findings.cloud_extension: Scovant Cloud fetches robots.txt from multiple regions to catch geo-inconsistent policies.
findings.limitations: Only reachability and syntax are checked; per-agent policy is evaluated by the other CORE-ACCESS checks.
findings.remediation: Scope Disallow rules to specific paths instead of blocking `/` for `*`.
findings.summary: robots.txt disallows all crawlers from the entire site.
findings.title: robots.txt availability and syntax
findings.why_it_matters: robots.txt is the first document a crawler checks; a broken or unreachable one forces every crawler to guess.

findings.cloud_extension: Scovant Cloud observes whether these crawlers are actually admitted or challenged.
findings.limitations: Only the declared robots.txt policy is evaluated; whether the crawler is actually served is not observed.
findings.remediation: Allow search/retrieval crawlers (OAI-SearchBot, Claude-SearchBot, PerplexityBot, …) in robots.txt while keeping any training restrictions separate.
findings.summary: robots.txt declares every major search and answer-engine crawler as disallowed. User-triggered fetch agents blocked: ChatGPT-User, Claude-User, Perplexity-User, DuckAssistBot.
findings.title: AI search crawler policy
findings.why_it_matters: Search and answer engines only surface pages their crawlers are declared allowed to fetch.

findings.cloud_extension: Scovant Cloud observes whether training and search crawlers are actually treated differently in practice.
findings.limitations: Only the declared robots.txt policy is evaluated.
findings.remediation: Restrict only the training-purpose crawler tokens; leave search/retrieval crawlers allowed.
findings.summary: Search/retrieval crawlers are restricted together with training crawlers — intent unclear.
findings.title: Training vs. search crawler separation
findings.why_it_matters: A site that wants to opt out of AI training without also losing answer-engine visibility needs the two crawler classes declared separately.

findings.cloud_extension: Scovant Cloud validates every child sitemap in an index and samples the full URL count.
findings.limitations: Only the first-declared sitemap (or its first child, for a sitemap index) is fetched and validated.
findings.remediation: Publish /sitemap.xml and declare it in robots.txt.
findings.summary: No sitemap was found.
findings.title: Sitemap availability
findings.why_it_matters: A sitemap is the most reliable way for a crawler to discover a site's full page inventory without following every link.

findings.cloud_extension: Scovant Cloud cross-checks lastmod against observed page changes over time.
findings.limitations: Only ISO 8601 date-formatted lastmod values are parsed; malformed dates are ignored, not penalised.
findings.summary: No valid sitemap to evaluate freshness for.
findings.title: Sitemap freshness
findings.why_it_matters: A stale or suspiciously uniform lastmod signal gives a crawler no reliable way to prioritise re-crawling changed pages.

findings.cloud_extension: Scovant Cloud validates canonical tags across every sampled page, not only the entry page.
findings.limitations: Only the entry page's declared canonical is evaluated.
findings.remediation: Point the canonical tag at a URL on this site's own host.
findings.summary: The canonical URL points off-host.
findings.title: Canonical URL integrity
findings.why_it_matters: A broken or off-host canonical tells agents the entry page's authoritative content lives somewhere else.

findings.cloud_extension: Scovant Cloud checks indexability across every sampled page.
findings.limitations: Only the entry page's own robots meta tag and X-Robots-Tag header are checked.
findings.remediation: Remove the noindex directive from the meta robots tag or X-Robots-Tag header.
findings.summary: The entry page declares noindex.
findings.title: Indexability
findings.why_it_matters: A page that declares noindex tells every compliant crawler, agents included, to leave it out of any index.

findings.cloud_extension: Scovant Cloud checks the supply-chain integrity of packages and hosts referenced from llms.txt.
findings.limitations: Absence is not penalised; the convention is emerging. Reference checks are HTTP status only.
findings.remediation: Remove or fix the broken references in llms.txt.
findings.summary: llms.txt references 1 link(s) that do not resolve.
findings.title: llms.txt presence and integrity
findings.why_it_matters: A well-formed llms.txt gives agents a curated map of the pages worth reading; a broken one sends them to dead links.

findings.cloud_extension: Scovant Cloud tracks Content-Signal adoption trends across the crawled corpus.
findings.limitations: Absence is not penalised; the convention is emerging.
findings.remediation: Fix the Content-Signal directive, e.g. "Content-Signal: search=yes, ai-input=yes, ai-train=no".
findings.summary: Content-Signal is declared but has syntax error(s).
findings.title: Content-Signal declaration
findings.why_it_matters: Content-Signal lets a site state search/AI-input/AI-training intent per dimension instead of leaving agents to guess from Disallow rules alone.

findings.cloud_extension: Scovant Cloud compares llms.txt against what agents actually fetch.
findings.limitations: Heuristics over the file text; a WARN is a prompt to review the file, not a defect. A bare `Disallow: /` in the robots.txt general (default) group does not itself count as an AI-crawler declaration for policy_misuse — only an allow/disallow entry declared under one of the registered AI agent tokens counts; a `Content-Signal:` directive can independently satisfy the same check. Experimental: never scored.
findings.summary: llms.txt links useful same-origin pages and carries no misplaced policy or template text.
findings.title: llms.txt utility
findings.why_it_matters: An llms.txt that links nothing useful, states crawler policy no crawler enforces, or is an untouched template gives agents nothing — adoption is not utility.

findings.cloud_extension: Scovant Cloud performs a live MCP handshake and enumerates the tool list, not just discovery-file presence.
findings.limitations: Only `/.well-known/mcp.json` and the two candidate server-card paths are probed; a custom discovery location is not found.
findings.summary: No MCP discovery file is published.
findings.title: MCP discovery presence
findings.why_it_matters: A published MCP discovery file (or server card) is how an agent finds this site's own tool interface instead of falling back to browser-shaped scraping.

findings.cloud_extension: Scovant Cloud performs a live handshake against each declared server and checks the declaration against the server's own runtime-reported identity.
findings.limitations: Only the `mcpServers` object at /.well-known/mcp.json is parsed; a server card is not covered by this check.
findings.summary: No MCP server is declared.
findings.title: MCP server declaration quality
findings.why_it_matters: An agent choosing among declared MCP servers needs a name, a URL, a transport, and a real description for each one — a bare, undescribed entry forces the agent to guess how to connect and why it should bother.

findings.cloud_extension: Scovant Cloud enumerates WebMCP tools in a real browser and checks state parity.
findings.limitations: This is a static text scan of already-fetched HTML for a marker string; the browser-side registration was not executed, so a marker's presence does not confirm the tools actually register or work.
findings.summary: No static WebMCP marker was found on the sampled pages.
findings.title: WebMCP static presence
findings.why_it_matters: A static WebMCP marker (an inline registration script, or a `<link rel="modelcontext">`/`<meta name="webmcp">` declaration) signals the page intends to expose in-browser tools to an agent.

findings.cloud_extension: Scovant Cloud enumerates WebMCP tools live in a real browser, seeing runtime-only definitions this static scan cannot.
findings.limitations: Static extraction of `registerTool(` calls in already-fetched HTML on the sampled pages; a runtime-only or dynamically-constructed tool definition is not seen.
findings.summary: No WebMCP tool registration was found on the sampled pages.
findings.title: WebMCP tool declaration quality
findings.why_it_matters: A WebMCP tool without a validated input schema, or without a description an agent can use to tell it apart from another, is unusable even though it registered.

findings.cloud_extension: Scovant Cloud validates the full OpenAPI document against the spec, not just that one parses.
findings.limitations: Only a fixed set of conventional paths, plus same-origin entry-page links naming openapi/swagger, are probed.
findings.summary: Not applicable to the commerce profile.
findings.title: OpenAPI discovery
findings.why_it_matters: A discoverable OpenAPI document lets an agent understand and call this API's surface directly instead of reverse-engineering it from prose docs.

findings.cloud_extension: Scovant Cloud exercises the discovered endpoints against a live OAuth flow, not just that the metadata document parses.
findings.limitations: Only the conventional /.well-known/oauth-authorization-server path is probed.
findings.summary: Not applicable to the commerce profile.
findings.title: OAuth authorization-server metadata
findings.why_it_matters: An agent that must authenticate to call this API needs RFC 8414 authorization-server metadata to discover the endpoints itself, rather than a human copying them out of docs.

findings.cloud_extension: Scovant Cloud exercises the discovered authorization server against a live OAuth flow, not just that the metadata document parses.
findings.limitations: Only the conventional /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource path is probed.
findings.summary: Not applicable to the commerce profile.
findings.title: OAuth protected-resource metadata
findings.why_it_matters: An agent that receives a 401 from a protected API needs RFC 9728 protected-resource metadata to discover which authorization server to talk to, instead of dead-ending.

findings.cloud_extension: Scovant Cloud exercises the UCP profile's declared services and capabilities against a live checkout flow.
findings.limitations: Only /.well-known/ucp is probed; a profile published at a non-conventional path is not found.
findings.remediation: Publish a valid UCP profile at /.well-known/ucp per the UCP specification.
findings.summary: A UCP profile is published but fails validation.
findings.title: UCP profile validity
findings.why_it_matters: An agent completing a purchase needs a machine-readable Universal Commerce Protocol profile naming this site's own services and capabilities, not just checkout copy.

findings.cloud_extension: Scovant Cloud validates each discovered surface's own schema, not just that a document is present.
findings.limitations: Only a fixed set of conventional well-known paths is probed; a custom discovery location is not found. A surface whose document could not be fetched or did not parse is indistinguishable here from one that is absent; this check therefore never reports WARN or ERROR.
findings.summary: Not applicable to the commerce profile.
findings.title: Agent discovery surface presence
findings.why_it_matters: A published agent discovery surface — an A2A agent card, an AI-plugin manifest, an agents.json, or an Agent Skills index — lets an agent find this service's own capabilities without a human pointing it there.

findings.cloud_extension: Scovant Cloud validates JSON-LD against the schema.org vocabulary, not just JSON syntax.
findings.limitations: Only well-formed-JSON parseability is checked; schema.org vocabulary correctness is not validated.
findings.remediation: Fix the malformed JSON-LD blocks so every one parses (validate with a JSON linter before publishing).
findings.summary: Some JSON-LD blocks on the sampled pages fail to parse as valid JSON.
findings.title: JSON-LD parseability
findings.why_it_matters: A structured-data block an agent's parser cannot read is worse than no block: it promises machine-readable data and then withholds it.

findings.cloud_extension: Scovant Cloud validates Organization data against the full schema.org vocabulary, not just presence of name/url.
findings.limitations: Only the schema_org nodes on the sampled pages are checked; an Organization declared elsewhere on the site is not evaluated.
findings.remediation: Add JSON-LD with "@type": "Organization" declaring at least name and url.
findings.summary: No Organization entity was found on the sampled pages.
findings.title: Organization entity
findings.why_it_matters: An agent trying to identify who operates a site (for trust, citation, or contact) needs a machine-readable Organization entity, not just a human-facing 'About' page.

findings.cloud_extension: Scovant Cloud checks WebSite/WebPage declarations across the full crawl, not just the sampled pages.
findings.limitations: Only the schema_org nodes on the sampled pages are checked.
findings.remediation: Add JSON-LD with "@type": "WebSite" or "WebPage".
findings.summary: No WebSite or WebPage entity was found on the sampled pages.
findings.title: WebSite/WebPage entity
findings.why_it_matters: A WebSite or WebPage entity anchors the rest of a site's structured data to a concrete machine-readable resource.

findings.cloud_extension: Scovant Cloud crawls the full product catalog rather than a bounded sample.
findings.limitations: Only the sampled pages are checked; a product catalog not represented in the sample is not evaluated.
findings.remediation: Add a stable identifier (sku, gtin, mpn, or brand) to the Product entity.
findings.summary: A Product entity exists but carries no identifiers.
findings.title: Product structured data
findings.why_it_matters: An agent completing a purchase needs a machine-readable Product entity with stable identifiers, not just human-facing catalog copy.

findings.cloud_extension: Scovant Cloud checks Offer completeness across the full sampled catalog, not just the first product page.
findings.limitations: Only the first sampled page that exposes a Product entity is checked.
findings.remediation: Add an Offer with price, priceCurrency, and availability to the Product entity.
findings.summary: The Product entity has no Offer with price, currency, or availability.
findings.title: Offer price, currency, and availability
findings.why_it_matters: An agent cannot decide whether to buy without knowing the price, currency, and stock status up front.

findings.cloud_extension: Scovant Cloud checks identifier coverage across the full sampled catalog, not just the pages in this scan.
findings.limitations: Only the sampled pages are checked; a product catalog not represented in the sample is not evaluated.
findings.remediation: Add a stable identifier (sku, gtin, mpn, or brand) to the Product entity.
findings.summary: Product entities declare no stable identifiers.
findings.title: Product identifier count
findings.why_it_matters: Two or more stable identifiers (sku, gtin, mpn, brand, ...) let an agent match the same product across catalogs and marketplaces with confidence; a single identifier is a weak, ambiguous match.

findings.cloud_extension: Scovant Cloud checks breadcrumb coverage across the full sampled catalog, not just the pages in this scan.
findings.limitations: Only the non-entry pages in the sampled set are checked.
findings.summary: Only the entry page was sampled; there are no additional pages to check for breadcrumbs.
findings.title: Breadcrumbs
findings.why_it_matters: A BreadcrumbList tells an agent where a page sits in a site's hierarchy without it having to infer structure from navigation markup.

findings.cloud_extension: Scovant Cloud checks metadata quality across every sampled page.

evidence.meta_description: A synthetic fixture site with several broken agent-readiness signals.
evidence.title: Example Bad Shop

findings.limitations: Only the entry page's metadata is checked.
findings.remediation: Add the missing metadata tags and give title and description distinct content.
findings.summary: The entry page's metadata has issues: og:title, og:description.
findings.title: Metadata quality
findings.why_it_matters: Title, description, and Open Graph tags are the first summary an agent (or a link preview) sees of a page.

findings.cloud_extension: Scovant Cloud checks heading structure across every sampled page.
findings.limitations: Only the entry page's heading outline is checked.
findings.remediation: Use exactly one H1 per page and avoid skipping heading levels (e.g. h1 to h3).
findings.summary: The entry page's heading structure has issues: multiple H1.
findings.title: Heading structure
findings.why_it_matters: A single, well-nested heading outline is how an agent (or a screen reader) infers a page's structure without reading every word.

findings.cloud_extension: Scovant Cloud checks the language declaration across every sampled page.
findings.limitations: Only the entry page's `<html lang>` attribute is checked.
findings.remediation: Add a valid `lang` attribute to the `<html>` tag (e.g. `lang="en"`).
findings.summary: The entry page's `lang` attribute is absent or invalid.
findings.title: Language declaration
findings.why_it_matters: A valid `lang` attribute lets an agent (or a translation/screen-reader tool) know what language a page's content is in without guessing.

findings.cloud_extension: Scovant Cloud checks image alt coverage across the full sampled catalog, not just the pages in this scan.
findings.limitations: Only the images on the sampled pages are counted.
findings.remediation: Add an alt attribute (or an explicit empty alt for decorative images) to every image.
findings.summary: Only 0/1 images have an alt attribute (ratio 0%).
findings.title: Image alt coverage
findings.why_it_matters: Alt text (or a deliberate empty/decorative alt) is how an agent that cannot see an image learns what it shows.

findings.cloud_extension: Scovant Cloud checks visible-vs-structured price agreement across the full sampled catalog and a broader set of currency formats.
findings.limitations: This is a fragile heuristic: the visible-price regex only matches a narrow set of currency-marked formats, and it compares only the first product page found.
findings.summary: No sampled page exposes a structured product price; evaluated by CORE-MACHINE-004/005.
findings.title: Visible vs. structured price
findings.why_it_matters: An agent that reads the structured price but a human-visible price disagrees will either quote the wrong number or abandon the page as untrustworthy.

findings.cloud_extension: Scovant Cloud renders a sample of pages in a real headless browser and compares the rendered content against the static fetch.
findings.limitations: Static-HTML signal only: the raw fetched response is inspected, never rendered in a browser, so a site that hydrates real content very quickly may still be flagged here.
findings.remediation: Server-render (or statically pre-render) the core content so an agent's plain HTTP fetch sees it.
findings.summary: The entry page's static HTML carries only 148 chars of visible text (< 200).
findings.title: Server-rendered core content
findings.why_it_matters: Most agent HTTP clients never execute JavaScript — if the core content only appears after client-side rendering, an agent reading the raw response sees an empty shell.

findings.cloud_extension: Scovant Cloud tracks redirect chains across every sampled page and over time.
findings.limitations: Only the entry URL's own redirect chain is inspected; redirects encountered while fetching other sampled pages are not counted here.
findings.remediation: Collapse the redirect chain to at most one hop.
findings.summary: The entry URL redirects 4 times before settling.
findings.title: Redirect chain complexity
findings.why_it_matters: Every redirect hop is a round trip an agent pays for before it reaches real content; a long or looping chain wastes budget CORE-ACCESS-001 already spent getting there.

findings.cloud_extension: Scovant Cloud checks cache-validator presence and correctness across the full sampled page set.
findings.limitations: Only the entry response's own headers are checked; per-page-type validator strategy is not inspected.
findings.remediation: Add an ETag or Last-Modified header so agents can issue conditional GETs.
findings.summary: The entry response carries no cache validator (ETag, Last-Modified, or Cache-Control).
findings.title: Cache validators
findings.why_it_matters: Without an ETag or Last-Modified, an agent revisiting a page can never issue a conditional GET — it re-downloads the full page every time.

findings.cloud_extension: Scovant Cloud checks a much larger set of machine-consumable endpoints and revisits them on a schedule.
findings.limitations: Only the capped set of references collected by the machine_links gatherer are checked; endpoints not linked from any declared document are not found. A declared MCP endpoint is recorded but never judged — Core does not perform the MCP handshake.
findings.remediation: Fix or remove the broken references (sitemap, llms.txt, OpenAPI spec, policy links) so agents don't hit dead links.
findings.summary: 2 of 2 machine-consumable reference(s) do not resolve.
findings.title: Broken machine-consumable endpoints
findings.why_it_matters: A declared machine reference that 404s wastes an agent's time and budget following a dead link the site itself pointed it at.

findings.cloud_extension: Scovant Cloud measures parse cost across the full sampled page set with a real BPE tokenizer.
findings.limitations: `estimated_tokens` is a character-count estimate (chars / token_chars_ratio), never a real tokenizer count, and only the entry page is measured.
findings.summary: The entry page's estimated parse cost is ~37 tokens (low).
findings.title: Agent parse cost
findings.why_it_matters: Every token of markup and script an agent parses before reaching real content is budget it can't spend understanding the page — a bloated entry page costs every agent that visits it, on every visit.

findings.cloud_extension: Scovant Cloud inspects forms across the full crawled page set, including those reachable only after interaction.
findings.limitations: Only forms on the sampled page set are inspected; a form behind client-side rendering that never appears in the static HTML is not seen.
findings.remediation: Add a <label> (or aria-label/aria-labelledby) to every input/select, and a name or accessible text to every button.
findings.summary: 1 control(s) across 1 form(s) lack a label or accessible name.
findings.title: Form/control labels
findings.why_it_matters: An agent filling out a form has to guess an unlabeled input's purpose from placeholder text or surrounding prose alone — a labeled control is the difference between a reliable fill and a guess.

findings.cloud_extension: Scovant Cloud resolves a larger reference surface on a recurring schedule and tracks resolution drift over time.
findings.limitations: Only references extracted from llms.txt and declared MCP server descriptions are resolved, under a hard per-scan lookup budget; a resolution that times out or exhausts the budget is recorded as unchecked, never as broken.
findings.summary: Machine reference integrity was not evaluated (experimental off).
findings.title: Machine reference integrity
findings.why_it_matters: A package name or domain named in agent-facing instructions that doesn't exist is a dependency-confusion / typosquat slot waiting to be claimed by someone else — an agent that follows the instruction inherits whatever fills it.

findings.cloud_extension: Scovant Cloud probes several unknown paths per host and per section, and re-checks over time.
findings.limitations: One extra request to a path that cannot exist (the URL is in evidence); a site that deliberately serves a 200 landing page for every path fails this check by design. The shell heuristic errs on the lenient side: a very short 200 page that carries a script bundle is reported as an application shell (WARN) even when it is in fact a terse, genuinely server-rendered soft-404.
findings.summary: Unknown paths answer with a real 404.
findings.title: Unknown paths return 404
findings.why_it_matters: An agent that receives HTTP 200 for a path that does not exist cannot tell a missing page from a real one; it may read an error template as content or cache a phantom URL.

findings.cloud_extension: Scovant Cloud observes rate-limit behaviour across its crawl and agent runs over time.
findings.limitations: Core never induces throttling; only 429 responses that happened to occur during the scan are examined, so most scans report N/A.
findings.summary: No 429 response was observed during this scan.
findings.title: Rate limiting is signalled
findings.why_it_matters: A 429 without Retry-After leaves an agent guessing when to come back; with it, a well-behaved agent backs off exactly as long as the server asks.

findings.cloud_extension: Scovant Cloud classifies WAF and challenge behaviour across identities and over time.
findings.limitations: Only the entry response and the sampled pages are inspected; a challenge served with an honest 403/429/503 is not a defect here (the access checks cover blocking).
findings.summary: No challenge page is served with HTTP 200.
findings.title: Challenge pages are not served as 200
findings.why_it_matters: A human-verification page returned with HTTP 200 is read by an agent as the page's content: it will summarise, quote or cache the challenge as if it were the site.

findings.cloud_extension: Scovant Cloud measures real agent discovery success across providers.
findings.limitations: Only llms.txt, OpenAPI, MCP and UCP are considered (a markdown-mirror surface and Link-header attribution are not yet wired into the Core evidence pipeline, so they cannot be checked). This check never fetches OpenAPI or UCP itself — it reads them only if another applicable check for this profile already gathered that evidence (OpenAPI: `CORE-INTERFACE-005`, profiles api/saas; UCP: `CORE-INTERFACE-008`, profile commerce). On any other profile, an unfetched OpenAPI/UCP surface is treated as not probed on this profile (counted as absent), never actively probed to find out — an unscored experimental check must never add its own network requests. Exactly two link sources are walked: the anchor links on the entry page itself, and the `machine_links` reference inventory — whose entries are sourced from the canonical URL, a policy-page link, the sitemap document URL itself, the declared OpenAPI spec, an MCP endpoint, or an llms.txt reference — matched only when one of those reference URLs equals a surface URL exactly. robots.txt directives and the URLs listed inside the sitemap are NOT scanned as a link source (the sitemap candidate above is the sitemap document URL itself, not a URL it lists). Experimental: never scored.
findings.remediation: Link llms.txt, OpenAPI, MCP and UCP documents from the entry page (e.g. a footer link), or reference them from the canonical URL, a policy page, or the OpenAPI spec.
findings.summary: 2 of 2 machine surface(s) are not linked from anything an agent reads: llms_txt, ucp.
findings.title: Discovery linkage
findings.why_it_matters: A machine surface an agent can only find by guessing a well-known path is discoverable in theory; one linked from the entry page or referenced by another already-gathered document is discoverable in practice. This measures declared, link-based discoverability — whether a real agent finds it is Scovant Cloud's measurement.

findings.cloud_extension: Scovant Cloud shows this finding in the Agentic Security & Trust section with regression tracking.
findings.limitations: Passive signal only. Scovant Core did not authenticate, submit forms or invoke tools; observed authorization behaviour is not tested.
findings.summary: Served over https; http:// redirects to https.
findings.title: HTTPS baseline
findings.why_it_matters: An agent that can be downgraded to plain HTTP can be read and rewritten in transit; the entry URL's scheme and the http→https redirect are the two externally observable signals.

findings.cloud_extension: Scovant Cloud shows this finding in the Agentic Security & Trust section with regression tracking.
findings.limitations: Passive signal only. Scovant Core did not authenticate, submit forms or invoke tools; observed authorization behaviour is not tested.
findings.remediation: Send Strict-Transport-Security: max-age=31536000 (add includeSubDomains once every subdomain is https).
findings.summary: No Strict-Transport-Security header.
findings.title: HSTS presence
findings.why_it_matters: Strict-Transport-Security keeps a returning agent on https even when it is handed an http:// link.

findings.cloud_extension: Scovant Cloud shows this finding in the Agentic Security & Trust section with regression tracking.
findings.limitations: Passive signal only. Scovant Core did not authenticate, submit forms or invoke tools; observed authorization behaviour is not tested.
findings.remediation: Send a Content-Security-Policy with frame-ancestors, or at least X-Frame-Options: DENY.
findings.summary: Neither Content-Security-Policy nor X-Frame-Options is sent.
findings.title: Content-Security-Policy / framing policy
findings.why_it_matters: A framing policy stops a page being embedded and click-jacked; a CSP is the declared allow-list agents can read. Neither alone proves XSS protection, and this check never claims it.

findings.cloud_extension: Scovant Cloud shows this finding in the Agentic Security & Trust section with regression tracking.
findings.limitations: Passive signal only. Scovant Core did not authenticate, submit forms or invoke tools; observed authorization behaviour is not tested.
findings.summary: No cookies set on the entry response.
findings.title: Security-relevant cookie attributes
findings.why_it_matters: A session-like cookie without Secure/HttpOnly/SameSite can be stolen or replayed by an agent-driven page; only names and attribute flags are inspected, never values.

findings.cloud_extension: Scovant Cloud shows this finding in the Agentic Security & Trust section with regression tracking.
findings.limitations: Passive signal only. Scovant Core did not authenticate, submit forms or invoke tools; observed authorization behaviour is not tested.
findings.remediation: Send Referrer-Policy: strict-origin-when-cross-origin and X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff.
findings.summary: Missing: referrer-policy, x-content-type-options.
findings.title: Referrer / MIME hygiene headers
findings.why_it_matters: Two low-cost headers that stop URL leakage and MIME sniffing; informational weight only.

findings.cloud_extension: Scovant Cloud shows this finding in the Agentic Security & Trust section with regression tracking.
findings.limitations: Passive signal only. Scovant Core did not authenticate, submit forms or invoke tools; observed authorization behaviour is not tested.
findings.remediation: Set Expires to a future date (RFC 3339) and keep it fresh.
findings.summary: Expires is in the past.
findings.title: security.txt validity (RFC 9116)
findings.why_it_matters: An expired or mis-located security.txt sends a reporter (human or agent) to a dead contact; CORE-TRUST-006 reports presence, this check reports validity.

findings.cloud_extension: Scovant Cloud tests observed data minimisation with synthetic identities.
findings.limitations: Passive signal only. Scovant Core reports declaration and exposure in public machine-facing documents; it never tests exploitability, authenticates or invokes tools.
findings.summary: No credential-like values in the gathered machine-facing surfaces.
findings.title: Credential-like value exposed in a machine-facing surface
findings.why_it_matters: llms.txt, discovery files and schemas are read verbatim by agents; a live key there is copied into every agent's context window.

findings.cloud_extension: Scovant Cloud tests observed data minimisation with synthetic identities.
findings.limitations: Passive signal only. Scovant Core reports declaration and exposure in public machine-facing documents; it never tests exploitability, authenticates or invokes tools.
findings.summary: No internal network references found.
findings.title: Internal network reference exposed
findings.why_it_matters: Private addresses, metadata endpoints and internal hostnames in public documents map the inside of a deployment; not a vulnerability by itself, hence low severity.

findings.cloud_extension: Scovant Cloud tests observed data minimisation with synthetic identities.
findings.limitations: Passive signal only. Scovant Core reports declared MCP server names and OpenAPI paths; the privileged/destructive classification is a NAME-BASED GUESS, never an inspection of actual behaviour, and it never authenticates, invokes a tool or submits a request.
findings.summary: No agent-facing interface declarations gathered.
findings.title: Privileged endpoint advertised to agents
findings.why_it_matters: An agent-facing declaration of an admin or destructive interface invites its use; Core reports the declaration only.

findings.cloud_extension: Scovant Cloud tests observed data minimisation with synthetic identities.
findings.limitations: Passive signal only. Scovant Core reports declared OpenAPI schema field names and their example/default values; it never authenticates, invokes an endpoint or submits a request.
findings.summary: No machine schema gathered.
findings.title: Sensitive field advertised in a machine schema
findings.why_it_matters: A schema that names a password field is normal; one that ships a sample or real value for it is a leak. The classification distinguishes the three.

findings.cloud_extension: Scovant Cloud runs authorized prompt-resilience scenarios with synthetic canaries.
findings.limitations: Heuristic passive indicator only: pattern matches over public machine-facing text. It never executes an instruction, never tests a real agent, and a WARN is not a vulnerability claim.
findings.summary: No indicators found.
findings.title: Hidden machine-facing imperative instructions
findings.why_it_matters: Text a human never sees but an agent reads verbatim is the classic indirect-injection carrier.

findings.cloud_extension: Scovant Cloud runs authorized prompt-resilience scenarios with synthetic canaries.
findings.limitations: Heuristic passive indicator only: pattern matches over public machine-facing text. It never executes an instruction, never tests a real agent, and a WARN is not a vulnerability claim.
findings.summary: No indicators found.
findings.title: Sensitive-information request instruction
findings.why_it_matters: A machine-facing request to disclose credentials or private data is the exfiltration half of an injection.

findings.cloud_extension: Scovant Cloud runs authorized prompt-resilience scenarios with synthetic canaries.
findings.limitations: Heuristic passive indicator only: pattern matches over public machine-facing text. It never executes an instruction, never tests a real agent, and a WARN is not a vulnerability claim.
findings.summary: No indicators found.
findings.title: External transmission instruction
findings.why_it_matters: An instruction to send data to a third-party host is a data-exfiltration attempt if an agent obeys it.

findings.cloud_extension: Scovant Cloud runs authorized prompt-resilience scenarios with synthetic canaries.
findings.limitations: Heuristic passive indicator only: pattern matches over public machine-facing text. It never executes an instruction, never tests a real agent, and a WARN is not a vulnerability claim.
findings.summary: No indicators found.
findings.title: Policy/role override language
findings.why_it_matters: "Ignore previous instructions" and friends have no legitimate place in site content.

findings.cloud_extension: Scovant Cloud runs authorized prompt-resilience scenarios with synthetic canaries.
findings.limitations: Heuristic passive indicator only: compares an instruction phrase found in machine-facing text against the visible text of the rendered page (itself capped at 5000 characters) by normalized substring containment. It never executes an instruction, never tests a real agent, and a WARN is not a vulnerability claim.
findings.summary: No indicators found.
findings.title: Human ↔ machine instruction divergence
findings.why_it_matters: Instructions present in the machine mirror but absent from the visible page are addressed to agents only.

findings.cloud_extension: Scovant Cloud runs authorized prompt-resilience scenarios with synthetic canaries.
findings.limitations: Heuristic passive indicator only: pattern matches over declared MCP server and WebMCP tool descriptions. It never executes an instruction, never invokes a tool, and a WARN is not a vulnerability claim.
findings.summary: No MCP server or WebMCP tool descriptions gathered.
findings.title: Tool/server description trust risk
findings.why_it_matters: A tool description is injected into the agent's context on every call; unrelated instructions or hidden Unicode there are a supply-chain injection vector.

findings.cloud_extension: Scovant Cloud checks contact reachability across the full sampled page set, not only the entry page.
findings.limitations: Only the entry page's anchors are scanned; a contact method reachable only from a deeper page is not found.
findings.remediation: Add a clearly labeled contact or support link (a page or a mailto link) to the entry page.
findings.summary: No contact or support link found on the entry page.
findings.title: Contact/support discoverability
findings.why_it_matters: An agent acting on a user's behalf needs a way to escalate to a human — a contact, support, or mailto link — when it hits a case it cannot resolve itself.

findings.cloud_extension: Scovant Cloud crawls the full sampled page set for a shipping-policy link, not only the entry page.
findings.limitations: Only a same-origin link discovered from the entry page's nav/footer/anchors is followed; a shipping policy reachable only from a deeper page is not found.
findings.remediation: Publish a shipping policy page (cost, timing, carriers) and link it from the entry page's nav or footer.
findings.summary: No shipping policy page was found linked from the entry page.
findings.title: Shipping policy discoverability
findings.why_it_matters: An agent completing a purchase on a user's behalf needs to know shipping cost and timing before it commits to checkout — a missing or unreadable shipping policy forces it to guess or abandon the order.

findings.cloud_extension: Scovant Cloud crawls the full sampled page set for a returns-policy link, not only the entry page.
findings.limitations: Only a same-origin link discovered from the entry page's nav/footer/anchors is followed; a returns policy reachable only from a deeper page is not found.
findings.remediation: Publish a returns/refund policy page and link it from the entry page's nav or footer.
findings.summary: No returns/refund policy page was found linked from the entry page.
findings.title: Returns/refund policy discoverability
findings.why_it_matters: An agent purchasing on a user's behalf needs to know whether and how a purchase can be returned before it commits — a missing or unreadable returns policy is a real trust gap, not a cosmetic one.

findings.cloud_extension: Scovant Cloud crawls the full sampled page set for a privacy-policy link, not only the entry page.
findings.limitations: Only a same-origin link discovered from the entry page's nav/footer/anchors is followed; a privacy policy reachable only from a deeper page is not found.
findings.remediation: Publish a privacy policy page and link it from the entry page's nav or footer.
findings.summary: No privacy policy page was found linked from the entry page.
findings.title: Privacy policy discoverability
findings.why_it_matters: An agent (and the human on whose behalf it acts) needs to know what data a site collects and how it is used before submitting any personal or payment information — a site with no privacy page at all is a real defect, not an omission.

findings.cloud_extension: Scovant Cloud crawls the full sampled page set for a terms/conditions link, not only the entry page.
findings.limitations: Only a same-origin link discovered from the entry page's nav/footer/anchors is followed; terms reachable only from a deeper page are not found.
findings.remediation: Publish a terms/conditions page and link it from the entry page's nav or footer.
findings.summary: No terms/conditions page was found linked from the entry page.
findings.title: Terms/conditions discoverability
findings.why_it_matters: An agent transacting with a site — buying, subscribing, or calling an API — needs the terms it is agreeing to on behalf of a user to be readable, not buried behind a broken or missing link.

findings.cloud_extension: Scovant Cloud validates the full RFC 9116 field set (Canonical, Encryption, Preferred-Languages), not only Contact and Expires.
findings.limitations: Only the conventional /.well-known/security.txt and legacy /security.txt paths are probed.
findings.remediation: Add a Contact field (RFC 9116) to security.txt.
findings.summary: security.txt was found but has no Contact field.
findings.title: security.txt discoverability
findings.why_it_matters: A security researcher — human or an automated scanner — needs a documented way to report a vulnerability; an agent auditing a site's operational maturity reads security.txt as that signal.

findings.cloud_extension: Scovant Cloud checks pricing across the full sampled page set and renders client-side pricing widgets to verify agent-visibility.
findings.limitations: Pricing-page discovery follows only a same-origin link from the entry page; the structured-price fallback checks only the sampled pages.
findings.summary: No pricing signal (a pricing page or a structured product price) was found.
findings.title: Pricing discoverability
findings.why_it_matters: An agent comparing options or completing a purchase on a user's behalf needs a readable price — one it can extract as text or structured data, not one rendered only by client-side script.
